title: Traumatic brain injury and concussion in the hospital
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the head injury (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/18/2026
Reason for Admission: Fall from ladder with head trauma.

Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 74, SpO2 98% on room air, Temp 98.6 F.
Recent Labs: WBC 8.4, Hgb 14.2, Plt 210, Na 139, K 4.1, Creatinine 0.9.

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Negative for fever, chills, or weight changes.
Neurological: Positive for headache and dizziness. Negative for focal weakness, numbness, or vision changes.
Cardiovascular: Negative for chest pain or palpitations.
Respiratory: Negative for shortness of breath or cough.
Musculoskeletal: Positive for neck pain. Negative for joint swelling.

Social History: Patient works as a construction foreman. He lives with his spouse and two children. He denies tobacco use.

Family History: Father had hypertension. Mother had type 2 diabetes. No family history of neurological disorders.

History of Present Illness:
[Copied Forward]: The patient is a 51-year-old male who presented to the emergency department following a fall from a ladder at a job site. He reports that he struck his head during the descent. He stated he did not lose consciousness at any time during the event. He complained of a persistent headache and mild disorientation immediately following the fall.

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted for observation and neuroimaging following a fall. Initial neurological examinations were stable. MRI of the head revealed a diffuse axonal injury. The patient remained stable throughout the stay, with no evidence of worsening neurological status. He was managed with headache management and activity restrictions. He tolerated a transition to a regular diet and was able to ambulate with minimal assistance. He is cleared for discharge with instructions to monitor for worsening symptoms.

Discharge Diagnoses:
- Diffuse axonal injury
- Traumatic brain injury

Discharge Medications:
- Acetaminophen 650mg every 6 hours as needed for pain.
- Multivitamin daily.

Follow-up:
Follow-up with neurology in 14 days for a repeat neurological exam and assessment of cognitive function.

Electronically signed, J. Lindqvist, MD, 05/18/2026
explanations: Diffuse traumatic brain injury without loss of consciousness, initial encounter: S06.2X0A (HCC 399).

distractors.why: No loss of consciousness is documented.

hccs.label: Major Head Injury without Loss of Consciousness
